evidence: Authored interoperability tests extending existing offline current-state and service contracts; no controller execution

sources.topic: CURJPOS nine-slot results, supplied current state, groups and model-derived pose
Joint registers, model conversion signatures, explicit limits and loaded frame/tool context

implemented.inputs: Exact configured joint width or complete JOINTPOS9 with zero-only unused slots, normalized at model/limit boundaries
implemented.outputs: GET_JPOS_REG pads narrow stored joints without modifying bank representation; model POS2JOINT writes its exact width or padded nine slots
implemented.validation: Reject nonzero/uninitialized/nonfinite/Boolean padding, other widths and invalid output shapes before operation outputs; normal limit checks retained
implemented.limits: One-to-nine-axis explicit limits-only contexts persist with or without current state; DH limits remain in model rows
implemented.frames: Loaded-model reachability uses current frame/tool selection; valid host map changes/removals and selections survive save/load
implemented.groups: All robot queries/conversions/range checks use root caller group during linked routines

portable_choices: Nine-slot padding is an authored Pythonic convention rather than a native encoding or evidence of additional physical axes
Only exact model/limit width or JOINTPOS9 is accepted; nonzero extra axes are not discarded
No global implicit JOINTPOS assignment conversion; custom callbacks without a model retain exact output width
Frame/tool IDs are portable 0..32767 integers; stored matrices and active selections are validated before persistence
Unchanged input representations and omitted default identity entries keep their original configuration shape
Bounded model math and limit checks do not establish collision clearance or native reachability
remaining: Native unused-axis encodings, external ABI and grouped storage layouts
